prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

A urine collection catheter is provided. The catheter includes: a conduit having an open distal end; a drainage tube positioned at least partially within the conduit; and a bladder superior wall support. The drainage tube includes one or more fluid ports or perforations for permitting fluid flow into a drainage lumen defined by the drainage tube. The bladder superior wall support includes a support cap and a plurality of support members extending from a proximal surface of the support cap through the open distal end of the conduit. The support cap is capable of being moved between a retracted position and a deployed position. In the deployed position, the distal end of the drainage tube is spaced apart from the support cap, such that the support cap supports portions of the superior wall of the bladder from occluding the one or more fluid ports or perforations of the drainage tube.

outputs.L2: A urine drainage catheter is described. The drainage tube has one or more fluid openings or perforations that allow liquid to enter a drainage lumen formed within the drainage tube. outputs.L3:
A urine collection catheter includes a conduit having an open distal end configured for placement within a bladder. A drainage tube is positioned at least partially within the conduit and defines a drainage lumen through which urine or other fluid may be removed from the bladder.

The drainage tube includes one or more fluid ports or perforations. These openings are arranged to allow fluid within the bladder to enter the drainage lumen and then pass through the drainage tube for collection or disposal.

The catheter further includes a bladder superior wall support. The bladder superior wall support includes a support cap and a plurality of support members that extend through the open distal end of the conduit. The support members help position and maintain the support cap relative to the drainage tube when the catheter is in use.

In a deployed position, the support cap is arranged to support or space portions of the bladder’s superior wall away from the drainage tube. By doing so, the support cap helps prevent the bladder wall from collapsing onto, covering, or otherwise occluding the fluid ports or perforations of the drainage tube. This configuration promotes continued fluid flow into the drainage lumen and reduces the likelihood of drainage blockage during urine collection.
outputs.L4:
A urine collection catheter is provided for facilitating drainage of urine from a patient’s bladder while reducing the likelihood that bladder tissue will obstruct the catheter’s drainage openings. The catheter includes an elongate conduit configured for insertion through the urethra and into the bladder. An internal drainage tube extends through at least a portion of the conduit and includes one or more fluid ports positioned near a distal end of the catheter. These fluid ports allow urine within the bladder to enter the drainage tube and be conducted away from the body to a collection receptacle or other drainage system.

The catheter further includes a deployable bladder superior wall support positioned near the distal end of the device. In an undeployed configuration, the support is arranged to permit insertion of the catheter with a reduced profile. After the distal end of the catheter is properly positioned within the bladder, the support may be deployed to form a support cap or similar structure. When deployed, the support cap engages or approaches the superior wall of the bladder and holds that wall spaced apart from the drainage tube and its fluid ports.

By maintaining separation between the bladder wall and the drainage ports, the deployed support helps prevent the ports from becoming occluded by tissue contact, suction effects, or collapse of the bladder wall around the catheter during drainage. This configuration promotes a more reliable flow path for urine into the drainage tube and can help maintain continuous or improved bladder drainage. The support may be designed to provide sufficient spacing without causing undue pressure or irritation to bladder tissue, and it may be returned to a lower-profile configuration to allow removal of the catheter when drainage is complete or replacement is required.

In use, the catheter is inserted in a conventional manner until the distal portion containing the drainage ports is located inside the bladder. The deployable support is then actuated to expand or otherwise assume its supporting shape. Urine enters the drainage tube through the fluid ports and flows through the conduit to an external collection device. Because the support cap holds the bladder wall away from the ports, the catheter is less susceptible to blockage caused by tissue obstruction, thereby improving drainage performance and reducing the need for repositioning, flushing, or replacement due to occlusion.
outputs.L5:
**The Power of “The”**

“The” may be one of the smallest words in the English language, but it is also one of the most important. It is called a definite article, and it helps us talk about specific people, places, objects, or ideas. For example, when we say “a book,” we could mean any book. But when we say “the book,” we are talking about one particular book that the listener or reader understands.

This simple word gives clarity and direction to sentences. It helps connect ideas and makes communication more precise. Without “the,” many sentences would feel incomplete or confusing. For instance, “I went to store” sounds unnatural, while “I went to the store” sounds clear and correct.

“The” is used every day in countless ways. We use it when talking about the sun, the world, the future, the past, and the people around us. Although it is short and often unnoticed, “the” plays a major role in shaping meaning.

In many ways, “the” proves that even the smallest words can have the greatest importance.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style abstract for a urine collection catheter with an internal drainage tube and a deployable cap that prevents the bladder wall from blocking the drainage ports.
counterfactuals.output: A urine collection catheter includes an elongate catheter body defining a drainage lumen and having one or more drainage ports near a distal end thereof. An internal drainage tube is disposed within the catheter body and communicates with the drainage lumen to convey urine from the bladder toward a proximal collection outlet. A deployable cap is carried at or adjacent the distal end of the catheter body and is movable between a collapsed delivery configuration and an expanded deployed configuration within the bladder. In the deployed configuration, the cap spaces bladder tissue away from the drainage ports and/or defines protected fluid pathways leading to the drainage ports, thereby inhibiting occlusion caused by contact between the bladder wall and the catheter. The cap may be biased toward the deployed configuration and may be actuated by insertion, fluid pressure, a control member, or withdrawal of a sheath. The catheter thereby maintains urine flow even when the bladder collapses around the distal end during drainage.

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a technical description of an invention: a catheter for urine drainage where a support cap deploys beyond the conduit to hold the superior bladder wall away from drainage openings.
counterfactuals.output:
A urinary drainage catheter includes an elongate tubular conduit defining a drainage lumen extending between a proximal drainage end and a distal insertion end. One or more drainage openings are formed through a wall of the conduit adjacent the distal insertion end and communicate with the drainage lumen for conducting urine from the bladder through the catheter.

The catheter further includes a deployable support cap disposed at or near the distal insertion end. The support cap is movable between a collapsed delivery configuration, in which the support cap has a reduced transverse profile suitable for passage through the urethra, and an expanded deployed configuration, in which the support cap extends radially and/or axially beyond the outer diameter of the conduit. When deployed within the bladder, the support cap forms a spacing structure positioned superior to or beyond the drainage openings, thereby maintaining the superior wall of the bladder in spaced relation from the drainage openings.

In use, the catheter is advanced into the bladder while the support cap is in the collapsed configuration. After the distal portion of the catheter enters the bladder, the support cap is deployed by an actuator, release mechanism, inflation mechanism, shape-memory recovery, or other deployment mechanism. In the deployed configuration, the support cap provides a broad, atraumatic support surface that contacts or approaches the superior bladder wall and prevents the bladder wall from collapsing directly onto the drainage openings during drainage. This reduces the likelihood of mucosal occlusion, suction trauma, intermittent blockage, incomplete drainage, and discomfort.

The support cap may be formed as a flexible umbrella-like member, mesh dome, cage, plurality of resilient ribs, inflatable cap, shape-memory frame, perforated canopy, or other expandable structure. The cap may include openings or channels to permit urine flow around and through the cap toward the drainage openings. The drainage openings may be positioned below, proximal to, or circumferentially around the base of the support cap so that urine can enter the drainage lumen while the cap maintains a protective separation between the bladder wall and the openings.

In some embodiments, the support cap is coupled to a distal tip of the conduit and expands outwardly from the distal tip after insertion. In other embodiments, the support cap is mounted on an inner shaft movable relative to the conduit, such that axial movement of the shaft causes the cap to expand or collapse. The catheter may further include a retention balloon, anchoring structure, or other bladder-retention feature located proximally of the support cap. The support cap and retention feature may cooperate to maintain catheter position while preserving a drainage space around the drainage openings.

The support cap is preferably made from biocompatible materials such as silicone, polyurethane, thermoplastic elastomer, nitinol, or combinations thereof. Portions of the cap may be soft, rounded, and atraumatic to avoid irritation of the bladder mucosa. The conduit may include a drainage lumen and, optionally, one or more additional lumens for balloon inflation, cap actuation, irrigation, pressure sensing, or drug delivery.

The invention thereby provides a urinary catheter that promotes continuous drainage by mechanically preventing the superior bladder wall from obstructing the catheter drainage openings, particularly when the bladder is partially or substantially emptied.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: In patent application language, describe a urine collection catheter that has an open distal conduit end, a drainage lumen with fluid ports, and a retractable/deployable bladder wall support structure.
counterfactuals.output:
In some embodiments, a urine collection catheter comprises an elongate catheter body extending between a proximal end portion and a distal end portion, the catheter body defining a drainage lumen extending therethrough. The distal end portion includes an open distal conduit end in fluid communication with the drainage lumen. A plurality of fluid ingress ports are formed through a sidewall of the catheter body at one or more locations proximal of the open distal conduit end, the plurality of fluid ingress ports being configured to admit urine from a bladder into the drainage lumen for conveyance toward the proximal end portion.

The catheter further includes a bladder wall support structure coupled to or carried by the distal end portion of the catheter body. The bladder wall support structure is movable between a retracted configuration and a deployed configuration. In the retracted configuration, the bladder wall support structure has a reduced transverse profile to facilitate insertion of the distal end portion through a urethra and into the bladder. In the deployed configuration, the bladder wall support structure extends radially outwardly relative to the catheter body to contact, space, support, or otherwise bias adjacent bladder wall tissue away from at least one of the open distal conduit end and the fluid ingress ports, thereby maintaining a fluid flow path into the drainage lumen and reducing obstruction of urine drainage by mucosal tissue.

In certain embodiments, the bladder wall support structure comprises one or more flexible struts, arms, loops, petals, ribs, mesh elements, expandable frames, or resilient members disposed about the distal end portion of the catheter body. The support structure may be self-expanding, mechanically actuated, elastically biased, or selectively deployable by relative movement of an actuator, sheath, stylet, pull wire, control member, or sleeve associated with the catheter. The support structure may be configured to assume the deployed configuration within the bladder after the distal end portion has passed through the urethra, and to return to the retracted configuration to permit removal of the catheter.

In some embodiments, the open distal conduit end provides an end-facing drainage opening, while the plurality of fluid ports provide side-facing drainage openings. The bladder wall support structure may be positioned distally of, proximally of, or at least partially surrounding the plurality of fluid ports, and may define one or more spaces or channels through which urine can pass to the ports and/or to the open distal conduit end. The deployed support structure may maintain the distal end portion in a spaced relationship from the bladder wall, inhibit suction adherence of the catheter to bladder tissue, and provide continued drainage even when one or more of the fluid ports are partially blocked.

In one example, the support structure includes a plurality of resilient arms having fixed ends secured to the catheter body and free or movable portions that bow outwardly when unconstrained. A retractable outer sleeve may be advanced over the arms to hold the arms in the retracted configuration and withdrawn to permit the arms to expand into the deployed configuration. In another example, a pull member extending through or along the catheter body is operable to foreshorten an expandable frame, thereby urging the frame radially outwardly into engagement with bladder wall tissue. Release of the pull member permits the frame to elongate and collapse toward the catheter body.

The drainage lumen may be connectable at the proximal end portion to a urine collection receptacle, suction source, drainage tubing, or valve. The catheter body and bladder wall support structure may be formed from biocompatible polymeric, elastomeric, metallic, or composite materials, including silicone, polyurethane, nylon, stainless steel, nitinol, or combinations thereof. The support structure may include atraumatic surfaces, rounded distal edges, radiopaque markers, coatings, or hydrophilic treatments to facilitate placement and reduce tissue irritation.

In use, the catheter is introduced with the bladder wall support structure in the retracted configuration and the distal end portion positioned within the bladder. The bladder wall support structure is then deployed to establish a spacing interface between the catheter and the bladder wall. Urine enters the catheter through the open distal conduit end and through the plurality of fluid ports, flows into the drainage lumen, and is conveyed proximally for collection. Prior to removal, the bladder wall support structure is returned to the retracted configuration, permitting withdrawal of the catheter through the urethra.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Create an abstract for a medical device patent covering a catheter that prevents occlusion of drainage perforations by using a cap and support members to support the bladder’s superior wall.
counterfactuals.output: A catheter for draining fluid from a urinary bladder includes an elongated tubular body having a drainage lumen and a distal portion configured for placement within the bladder. The distal portion includes one or more drainage perforations in fluid communication with the drainage lumen. A cap is disposed at or adjacent a distal end of the tubular body, and a plurality of support members extend from the distal portion and/or the cap to engage and support a superior wall of the bladder when the catheter is positioned for use. The support members maintain spacing between bladder tissue and the drainage perforations, thereby reducing tissue collapse over the perforations and preventing or limiting occlusion during drainage. In some embodiments, the support members are resilient, expandable, collapsible, or atraumatic to facilitate insertion, deployment, and removal of the catheter while maintaining an open drainage path.
